claims.text: Closed-door briefing at the Capitol lasting about 90 minutes at which ICIG Thomas Monheim spoke with House Oversight and Accountability Committee members, intended to improve transparency around the government's knowledge of UAP.
Burchett: 'At one time, we had 16 congressmen in there... And these were people that normally you wouldn't see,' naming Moskowitz, Ocasio-Cortez and Luna; he rated the briefing four out of ten.
Ogles emerged saying what 'most Americans fear is true,' describing 'a concerted effort to conceal as much information as possible - both in Congress and to the general public.'

desc: A roughly ninety-minute closed-door briefing at the Capitol on 12 January 2024 at which Intelligence Community Inspector General Thomas Monheim met House Oversight and Accountability members and members of the Congressional UAP Caucus. Burchett said around sixteen members attended - 'the whole gang' - naming Moskowitz, Ocasio-Cortez and Luna. What the briefing produced is a bipartisan null. Krishnamoorthi: 'I didn't get the answers that I was hoping for.' Burchett: 'more of the same... it's very compartmentalized; it's like looking down the barrel of a .22 rifle... now it's just whack-a-mole,' rating it four out of ten. Ogles: 'I asked very specific questions and was unable to get specific answers.' Burlison and Garcia were more positive, describing direction and new information respectively. This is the only formal encounter between the House and the watchdog whose credible-and-urgent finding on the Grusch complaint is the legal foundation of the entire inquiry, and it did not resolve any substantive question the committee had asked.
